name: Akthi, the Final Sting
description: A named enemy that holds the Khari Crossing, fought in the interlude content that sits between the main acts rather than on the critical path of a single act.

beginner.whatItIs: A named enemy that holds the Khari Crossing, fought in the interlude content that sits between the main acts rather than on the critical path of a single act.
beginner.whyItMatters: It carries resistance to fire, lightning and physical damage at once and takes extra punishment from cold, so it quietly checks whether your damage has any flexibility at all.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Take it on when the Khari Crossing opens up. If your only damage is fire, lightning or physical, expect a slow grind and consider swapping in a cold source first.

name: Anundr, the Sandworm
description: A burrowing desert monster fought at the Khari Crossing during the interlude content between acts.

beginner.whatItIs: A burrowing desert monster fought at the Khari Crossing during the interlude content between acts.
beginner.whyItMatters: It has no listed resistance at all and takes extra damage from both lightning and physical hits, which makes it a rare chance to simply push your damage buttons and watch a health bar move.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Good to attempt on the level you first reach the Khari Crossing. A physical or lightning weapon build clears it quickly.

name: Ashar, the Sand Mother
description: A level 60 boss inside the Trial of the Sekhemas, one of the two trial lines that hand out ascendancy points. It fights with claws, a poison slam, two different tail attacks, and a burrow it uses to reposition.

beginner.whatItIs: A level 60 boss inside the Trial of the Sekhemas, one of the two trial lines that hand out ascendancy points. It fights with claws, a poison slam, two different tail attacks, and a burrow it uses to reposition.
beginner.whyItMatters: Trial bosses gate the passive points that turn your class into its specialisation, so this is progression rather than optional content. The burrow also means your damage window closes and reopens on the fight's schedule, not yours.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Bring it a character at or above level 60 with chaos or poison mitigation. Save your movement skill for the moment it surfaces from the burrow rather than spending it early.

name: Asinia, the Praetor's Consort
description: A level 9 Act 1 boss found in the Tomb of the Consort, a side area rather than a required stop on the campaign route.

beginner.whatItIs: A level 9 Act 1 boss found in the Tomb of the Consort, a side area rather than a required stop on the campaign route.
beginner.whyItMatters: It is one of the earlier optional fights available, which makes it a low-risk place to learn how a boss arena behaves before the campaign starts demanding it of you.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Clear it around level 9 while you are already working through the Act 1 tombs. Skipping it costs you nothing on the main quest, but the practice is cheap.

name: Atziri, the Red Queen
description: A pinnacle-tier encounter fought in Atziri's Temple. She deals fire, lightning and physical damage and carries thirty percent resistance to fire, lightning and cold.

beginner.whatItIs: A pinnacle-tier encounter fought in Atziri's Temple. She deals fire, lightning and physical damage and carries thirty percent resistance to fire, lightning and cold.
beginner.whyItMatters: Her damage spans three different types, so stacking one defence will not carry the fight. The even thirty percent resistance across the elements means no elemental build is punished harder than another, but none of them get a free ride either.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Come to her once your elemental resistances are capped and you are comfortable reading multiple damage patterns at the same time, not while you are still fixing gear.

name: Aurelian, the Grand Adjudicator
description: The boss that sits at the end of the Digsite map, part of the endgame map layer that opens after the campaign. Map bosses are scaled to level 65 and above.

beginner.whatItIs: The boss that sits at the end of the Digsite map, part of the endgame map layer that opens after the campaign. Map bosses are scaled to level 65 and above.
beginner.whyItMatters: Killing the boss is what completes a map and pushes your atlas progress forward, so an endgame session is really a sequence of fights like this one.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Run it once you are into maps and your character is at least level 65. If a Digsite map rolls modifiers you cannot handle, reroll it rather than feeding it a portal.

name: Azarian, the Forsaken Son
description: A level 24 Act 2 boss in the Buried Shrines, fought during the Trail of Corruption quest. It deals physical and fire damage and resists fire.

beginner.whatItIs: A level 24 Act 2 boss in the Buried Shrines, fought during the Trail of Corruption quest. It deals physical and fire damage and resists fire.
beginner.whyItMatters: It is a required quest fight, so the campaign stops until it is dead. Its fire resistance means a fire build has to work harder here than the surrounding zone suggested.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Take it at level 24 or a little above with fire resistance on your gear. If your damage is fire-based, this is a good moment to have a second damage source available.

name: Azmadi, the Faridun Prince
description: A Faridun leader fought at the Qimah Reservoir in the interlude content between acts. He resists fire and physical damage.

beginner.whatItIs: A Faridun leader fought at the Qimah Reservoir in the interlude content between acts. He resists fire and physical damage.
beginner.whyItMatters: Resisting fire and physical at once covers two damage types that levelling characters lean on heavily, so this fight tends to run longer than the ones around it.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Attempt him when the Qimah Reservoir is on your route. Cold or lightning damage moves his health bar faster than a physical weapon will.

name: Bahlak, the Sky Seer
description: A level 40 and above boss in the Temple of Chaos, part of the Trial of Chaos ascendancy line. It uses swipes, a skydive, windbursts, feather sprays, ball lightning, cascading lightning, tornadoes, and an enrage that speeds it up.

beginner.whatItIs: A level 40 and above boss in the Temple of Chaos, part of the Trial of Chaos ascendancy line. It uses swipes, a skydive, windbursts, feather sprays, ball lightning, cascading lightning, tornadoes, and an enrage that speeds it up.
beginner.whyItMatters: It resists fire, lightning and physical damage while taking extra from cold, and the enrage means the fight gets harder the longer you take. Trial of Chaos bosses also stand between you and ascendancy points.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Go in at level 40 or higher with lightning resistance in place. Cold damage shortens the fight, which is the real counter to the enrage.

name: Balbala, the Traitor
description: An Act 2 boss in Traitor's Passage, fought during the Ascent to Power quest. She deals physical, chaos and fire damage and resists fire while taking extra from cold.

beginner.whatItIs: An Act 2 boss in Traitor's Passage, fought during the Ascent to Power quest. She deals physical, chaos and fire damage and resists fire while taking extra from cold.
beginner.whyItMatters: Chaos damage bypasses energy shield, so a build that leans on shield rather than life finds out here that part of its defence does not apply. The fight is a required quest step as well.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Fight her once chaos resistance is not deeply negative and you have a way to heal through damage over time. Cold damage is the fastest way out of the fight.

name: Beira of the Rotten Pack
description: A level 2 boss in Clearfell, one of the first named enemies a new character meets in Act 1. She deals physical and cold damage, resists cold, and takes extra from fire.

beginner.whatItIs: A level 2 boss in Clearfell, one of the first named enemies a new character meets in Act 1. She deals physical and cold damage, resists cold, and takes extra from fire.
beginner.whyItMatters: This is where the game first teaches that a boss has a resistance profile at all. Her cold damage can freeze a character with no cold resistance, which is many players' first hard stop.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Fight her at level 2 or 3 as part of the normal Act 1 route. Any fire source you have picked up so far will shorten it noticeably.

name: Benedictus, First Herald of Utopia
description: An Act 4 boss in the Excavation, fought during the Search quest. He deals physical and lightning damage, resists lightning, and fights with stone throws, pillar slams, lightning lashes, floating lightning stones and two different maze patterns that fill the arena with walls.

beginner.whatItIs: An Act 4 boss in the Excavation, fought during the Search quest. He deals physical and lightning damage, resists lightning, and fights with stone throws, pillar slams, lightning lashes, floating lightning stones and two different maze patterns that fill the arena with walls.
beginner.whyItMatters: The maze phases turn the arena itself into the threat, so this is a movement and positioning fight before it is a damage fight. He has no listed weakness to lean on.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Take him on with lightning resistance capped and a movement skill you have not already spent. Learn the wall patterns on a cheap attempt before committing your good portals.

name: Blackjaw, the Remnant
description: A level 37 Act 3 boss inside Jiquani's Machinarium. It resists fire and physical damage and takes extra from cold.

beginner.whatItIs: A level 37 Act 3 boss inside Jiquani's Machinarium. It resists fire and physical damage and takes extra from cold.
beginner.whyItMatters: Act 3 is where physical weapon damage on its own starts to run out of road, and a boss resisting both fire and physical is a clear signal that a second damage type is now worth carrying.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Around level 37, on the normal Act 3 route. If you have a cold skill gem sitting unused in your inventory, this is the fight to slot it for.

name: Brakka, the Withered Crone
description: The boss guarding the end of the Sump map in the endgame map layer, fought at level 65 and above.

beginner.whatItIs: The boss guarding the end of the Sump map in the endgame map layer, fought at level 65 and above.
beginner.whyItMatters: Endgame maps only count as completed once their boss is down, so this fight is the difference between a map that advances your atlas and one that does not.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Run it as part of normal map progression once you are past the campaign. Check the map's rolled modifiers before you enter, because they apply to the boss as well as the zone.

name: Brakkus, the Juggernaut
description: A heavy melee map boss found at the end of the Cliffside map, scaled to level 65 and above.

beginner.whatItIs: A heavy melee map boss found at the end of the Cliffside map, scaled to level 65 and above.
beginner.whyItMatters: A boss built around big physical hits punishes standing still, so it is a practical test of whether your defensive layers actually work when a slam lands rather than when you are dodging perfectly.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Once your character is comfortably into maps. Keep space between you and the arena walls so a charge cannot pin you.

name: Brughor, the Insatiable
description: The map boss of Rockpools, part of the endgame atlas content at level 65 and above.

beginner.whatItIs: The map boss of Rockpools, part of the endgame atlas content at level 65 and above.
beginner.whyItMatters: Map bosses drop the currency and item volume that funds an endgame build, so consistently killing them rather than skipping to the exit is what makes maps profitable.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Whenever a Rockpools map comes up in your atlas rotation. Clear the surrounding pack density first so you are not fighting the boss and a swarm at once.

name: Caedron, the Hyena Lord
description: A map boss that appears in both the Wetlands and Savannah maps, fought at level 65 and above.

beginner.whatItIs: A map boss that appears in both the Wetlands and Savannah maps, fought at level 65 and above.
beginner.whyItMatters: Because he shows up in two different map layouts, you will meet him repeatedly across an atlas run, so learning his pattern once pays off more than usual.
beginner.whenToUseIt: On any Wetlands or Savannah map. Expect adds alongside him and bring an area skill rather than a pure single-target setup.

name: Candlemass, the Living Rite
description: The level 15 boss of Ogham Manor in Act 1. It uses a cleave, a leap slam and a candle wave, deals physical and fire damage, and resists fire, cold and physical.

beginner.whatItIs: The level 15 boss of Ogham Manor in Act 1. It uses a cleave, a leap slam and a candle wave, deals physical and fire damage, and resists fire, cold and physical.
beginner.whyItMatters: Three resistances at once on a levelling boss means whatever you brought is partly blunted, which is the game's way of pushing you towards gear upgrades before the act ends.
beginner.whenToUseIt: At level 15 or above, once your fire resistance is not negative. Sidestep the leap slam rather than trying to outrun it in a straight line.

name: Captain Hartlin
description: A level 47 Act 4 boss at Journey's End, fought during the Dark Mists quest. He resists cold damage and has no listed weakness.

beginner.whatItIs: A level 47 Act 4 boss at Journey's End, fought during the Dark Mists quest. He resists cold damage and has no listed weakness.
beginner.whyItMatters: A quest boss with a resistance and no weakness gives you nothing to exploit, so the fight comes down to your own damage output and your ability to survive the pattern.
beginner.whenToUseIt: At level 47 or above with your gear actually upgraded for Act 4 rather than carried over from Act 3. A cold-damage build should expect a longer fight here.

name: Chetza, the Feathered Plague
description: A level 40 and above Trial of Chaos boss in the Temple of Chaos. It pecks, sprays vomit, spits projectiles, spirals with its beak, smashes with its face, calls a birdstorm, and summons plaguelings to fight alongside it.

beginner.whatItIs: A level 40 and above Trial of Chaos boss in the Temple of Chaos. It pecks, sprays vomit, spits projectiles, spirals with its beak, smashes with its face, calls a birdstorm, and summons plaguelings to fight alongside it.
beginner.whyItMatters: The summoned adds mean you cannot simply stand and focus the boss, and its cold resistance blunts a cold build while fire damage hits it harder. Clearing it is part of earning ascendancy points.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Enter at level 40 or above with an area skill for the plaguelings. Fire damage is the shortcut if you have any available.

name: Colm, the Rancorous
description: A map boss in the Woodland map at level 65 and above. He swipes, swings a log, sunders the ground, charges, and summons drowned enemies to join the fight.

beginner.whatItIs: A map boss in the Woodland map at level 65 and above. He swipes, swings a log, sunders the ground, charges, and summons drowned enemies to join the fight.
beginner.whyItMatters: The summoned drowned turn a single-target fight into a crowd fight, which is where builds with no area damage discover their gap in the middle of an endgame map.
beginner.whenToUseIt: On any Woodland map once you are in the endgame. Kill the summons before they stack up rather than trying to burst the boss through them.

name: Connal, the Tormented
description: The boss of the Willow map, part of the level 65 and above endgame map layer.

beginner.whatItIs: The boss of the Willow map, part of the level 65 and above endgame map layer.
beginner.whyItMatters: Willow is a map you will roll repeatedly during atlas progression, so this fight becomes routine, and a fight that becomes routine is where careless deaths happen.
beginner.whenToUseIt: During normal map running. Keep your flasks for the boss room instead of burning them on the trash on the way in.

name: Corrupted Abomination
description: A special encounter enemy that does not live in a fixed zone. It is spawned by activating an Ancient Beacon.

beginner.whatItIs: A special encounter enemy that does not live in a fixed zone. It is spawned by activating an Ancient Beacon.
beginner.whyItMatters: Beacon encounters are opt-in, so you choose when to face this. That makes it one of the few fights whose difficulty you can time to your own gear rather than to the campaign's pace.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Activate the beacon when you are already healthy and your cooldowns are up. There is no reason to trigger it while you are still clearing the area around you.

name: Count Geonor
description: The Act 1 finale at level 15 in the Iron Manor, and a level 79 rematch in the Iron Citadel. He deals physical and cold damage with slash combos, freezing thrusts, ice walls, ice breath, moonbeams, summoned werewolves and blood-fuelled attacks in the later phases.

beginner.whatItIs: The Act 1 finale at level 15 in the Iron Manor, and a level 79 rematch in the Iron Citadel. He deals physical and cold damage with slash combos, freezing thrusts, ice walls, ice breath, moonbeams, summoned werewolves and blood-fuelled attacks in the later phases.
beginner.whyItMatters: The two versions are a different fight: campaign Geonor has thirty percent cold resistance, while the Citadel version has seventy-five percent cold resistance and doubled freeze buildup. A cold build that walks over the first one can stall completely on the second.
beginner.whenToUseIt: The Act 1 version at level 15 or above with cold resistance on your gear. The Citadel version only once you are near level 79 and have real freeze avoidance, not just resistance.

name: Diamora, Song of Death
description: An Act 4 boss found in the Singing Caverns.

beginner.whatItIs: An Act 4 boss found in the Singing Caverns.
beginner.whyItMatters: Act 4 sits at the end of the campaign, where enemy damage assumes your resistances are capped and your weapon has been upgraded at least once since Act 3.
beginner.whenToUseIt: On the normal Act 4 route. If the fight feels impossible, the answer is almost always a gear check rather than a skill swap.

name: Doryani, Royal Thaumaturge
description: An Act 3 boss in the Black Chambers. He deals fire, cold, lightning and physical damage and carries thirty percent fire and lightning resistance plus physical resistance.

beginner.whatItIs: An Act 3 boss in the Black Chambers. He deals fire, cold, lightning and physical damage and carries thirty percent fire and lightning resistance plus physical resistance.
beginner.whyItMatters: He throws fire, cold, lightning and physical damage at you in the same fight, so a single missing resistance on your gear turns into the thing that kills you. This is the campaign's clearest argument for capping all three elements.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Once fire, cold and lightning resistance are all capped. Fixing a single resistance before this fight usually does more than any damage upgrade would.

name: Draven, the Eternal Praetor
description: A level 9 Act 1 boss in the Mausoleum of the Praetor, an optional side area off the main Act 1 route.

beginner.whatItIs: A level 9 Act 1 boss in the Mausoleum of the Praetor, an optional side area off the main Act 1 route.
beginner.whyItMatters: Optional early bosses are free experience and free item rolls at a point where a single upgrade changes how the whole act feels.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Around level 9, while you are already clearing the mausoleum. There is no quest pressure, so retreat and come back a level higher if it goes badly.

name: Ekbab, Ancient Steed
description: A level 25 Act 2 boss in the Bone Pits, fought as part of the Theft of Ivory quest.

beginner.whatItIs: A level 25 Act 2 boss in the Bone Pits, fought as part of the Theft of Ivory quest.
beginner.whyItMatters: It is a required quest kill, so Act 2 does not progress around it. Bone Pits also holds a second named boss, which means the zone asks for two boss-ready attempts rather than one.
beginner.whenToUseIt: At level 25 or above. Clear the zone first so you enter the fight with your flasks charged rather than empty.

name: Elzarah, the Cobra Lord
description: A named enemy in the Sel Khari Sanctuary, part of the interlude content between acts. It resists lightning and physical damage.

beginner.whatItIs: A named enemy in the Sel Khari Sanctuary, part of the interlude content between acts. It resists lightning and physical damage.
beginner.whyItMatters: Lightning and physical resistance together blunt two damage types most levelling weapons deal, so the fight rewards having a cold or fire option in reserve.
beginner.whenToUseIt: When the Sel Khari Sanctuary comes up on your route. Swap to a non-physical damage source if your health bar is moving faster than the boss's.

name: Gelida, the Frost-Tongue
description: A map boss found at the end of the Alpine Ridge map, in the endgame layer at level 65 and above.

beginner.whatItIs: A map boss found at the end of the Alpine Ridge map, in the endgame layer at level 65 and above.
beginner.whyItMatters: Alpine Ridge can also roll Ignatia as its boss, so the same map does not always end in the same fight. Knowing which one you are walking into changes what you prepare for.
beginner.whenToUseIt: On an Alpine Ridge map during atlas progression. Treat cold-themed arenas as a reason to check your cold resistance before entering.

name: Godwin of the Shattered Creed
description: A named enemy encountered at Holten in the interlude content between acts. He resists fire and physical damage and takes extra from cold.

beginner.whatItIs: A named enemy encountered at Holten in the interlude content between acts. He resists fire and physical damage and takes extra from cold.
beginner.whyItMatters: Holten holds more than one named fight, so the area asks you to arrive with resources rather than stumble in after a long clear.
beginner.whenToUseIt: When Holten is on your route. Lead with cold damage if you have it, since that is the one thing he does not shrug off.

name: Gorian, the Moving Earth
description: A map boss that can appear in either the Trenches or the Bloodwood map, in the endgame layer at level 65 and above.

beginner.whatItIs: A map boss that can appear in either the Trenches or the Bloodwood map, in the endgame layer at level 65 and above.
beginner.whyItMatters: Bosses that appear across two map layouts show up more often in an atlas run, so the time you spend learning this one gets repaid across several maps rather than one.
beginner.whenToUseIt: On any Trenches or Bloodwood map. Give yourself room to move before the fight starts, since a ground-slam pattern in a tight corner leaves nowhere to go.

name: Gozen, Rebellious Rustlord
description: The boss of the Rustbowl map at level 65 and above. He resists physical and fire damage and takes extra from lightning.

beginner.whatItIs: The boss of the Rustbowl map at level 65 and above. He resists physical and fire damage and takes extra from lightning.
beginner.whyItMatters: A map boss with a stated weakness is uncommon enough to be worth acting on, and a lightning source will visibly shorten this fight compared with a physical weapon.
beginner.whenToUseIt: On a Rustbowl map. If you carry a swap weapon or a second skill with lightning damage, this is the fight to bring it out for.

name: Great White One
description: A level 46 Act 4 boss on Whakapanu Island, fought as part of the Tribal Medicine quest. It resists cold and physical damage and takes extra from lightning.

beginner.whatItIs: A level 46 Act 4 boss on Whakapanu Island, fought as part of the Tribal Medicine quest. It resists cold and physical damage and takes extra from lightning.
beginner.whyItMatters: It sits on a quest, so the act does not move on without it, and its resistance profile blunts exactly the melee-plus-cold setup that many characters arrive in Act 4 running.
beginner.whenToUseIt: At level 46 or above. If your damage is physical or cold, bringing any lightning option turns a slog into a normal fight.

name: Gressor-Kul, the Apex
description: A map boss that shows up at the end of the Augury and Bluff maps, part of the endgame content at level 65 and above.

beginner.whatItIs: A map boss that shows up at the end of the Augury and Bluff maps, part of the endgame content at level 65 and above.
beginner.whyItMatters: Endgame maps are where a character stops levelling through the campaign and starts farming, and the boss is the part of the map that actually pays for the run.
beginner.whenToUseIt: During normal atlas progression on either of those maps. Enter the arena with your flask charges topped up rather than spent on the approach.

name: Grudgelash, Vile Ent
description: The boss of the Burial Bog map in the endgame layer, scaled to level 65 and above.

beginner.whatItIs: The boss of the Burial Bog map in the endgame layer, scaled to level 65 and above.
beginner.whyItMatters: Bog and swamp layouts tend to slow your movement, and a boss fight where you cannot reposition freely punishes builds that rely on constant repositioning to survive.
beginner.whenToUseIt: On a Burial Bog map once you are past the campaign. Clear a patch of open ground before pulling the boss into it.

name: Guardian Construct
description: One of the guardian enemies found inside Atziri's Temple, fought as an encounter rather than as a fixed campaign boss.

beginner.whatItIs: One of the guardian enemies found inside Atziri's Temple, fought as an encounter rather than as a fixed campaign boss.
beginner.whyItMatters: The temple stacks several of these encounters in one place, so your survivability has to hold across a sequence rather than through a single burst of damage.
beginner.whenToUseIt: While working through Atziri's Temple. Treat each construct as a full fight rather than as trash on the way to the queen.

name: Gulzal, the Living Furnace
description: The map boss of the Vaal Foundry, part of the endgame map layer at level 65 and above.

beginner.whatItIs: The map boss of the Vaal Foundry, part of the endgame map layer at level 65 and above.
beginner.whyItMatters: Foundry and forge arenas lean on fire damage, and an uncapped fire resistance in the endgame is the kind of gap that ends a run in one hit rather than gradually.
beginner.whenToUseIt: On a Vaal Foundry map, with fire resistance capped. Check the map's own modifiers first, since added elemental damage stacks on top of what the boss already deals.

name: Hadi of the Flaming River
description: A level 45 and above boss in the Trial of the Sekhemas, one of the two routes to ascendancy points. It fights with fist strikes, fist and foot slams, a shockwave step and an explosion.

beginner.whatItIs: A level 45 and above boss in the Trial of the Sekhemas, one of the two routes to ascendancy points. It fights with fist strikes, fist and foot slams, a shockwave step and an explosion.
beginner.whyItMatters: Every attack it has is a ground-based slam, so the fight is decided by where you stand rather than by how much damage you can pour into it. It is also a required step towards your ascendancy.
beginner.whenToUseIt: At level 45 or above, once you have honour and relic setup you are happy with. Keep moving between slams instead of standing to attack through them.

name: Hask, the Fallen Son
description: A map boss appearing in the Channel and Headland maps, in the endgame layer at level 65 and above.

beginner.whatItIs: A map boss appearing in the Channel and Headland maps, in the endgame layer at level 65 and above.
beginner.whyItMatters: Because he anchors two separate map layouts, he is one of the fights that defines what a normal atlas run feels like for you.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Whenever a Channel or Headland map comes up. Standard endgame preparation applies: capped resistances, a charged flask set, and an escape option off cooldown.

name: Heldra of the Black Pyre
description: A level 54 named enemy in the Scorched Farmlands, fought during the Recruit the Ezomytes interlude quest. She resists fire and takes extra from cold.

beginner.whatItIs: A level 54 named enemy in the Scorched Farmlands, fought during the Recruit the Ezomytes interlude quest. She resists fire and takes extra from cold.
beginner.whyItMatters: The Scorched Farmlands hold both Heldra and Isolde, and the two have opposite profiles, so a build that answers one may be blunted against the other.
beginner.whenToUseIt: At level 54 or above during the Ezomyte recruitment. Cold damage is the direct answer to her, and it is exactly the wrong tool for her counterpart.

name: High Priest
description: A named enemy that appears only when you activate an Ancient Beacon, rather than in any fixed zone.

beginner.whatItIs: A named enemy that appears only when you activate an Ancient Beacon, rather than in any fixed zone.
beginner.whyItMatters: Beacon spawns are triggered by you, which means the encounter is optional and its timing is entirely under your control.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Trigger the beacon when you are at full health with your defensive cooldowns available. There is no reward for lighting it while you are already in trouble.

name: Ignagduk, the Bog Witch
description: A level 36 Act 3 boss in the Azak Bog, fought during the Tribal Vengeance quest. She deals physical and fire damage, resists fire, and takes extra from cold.

beginner.whatItIs: A level 36 Act 3 boss in the Azak Bog, fought during the Tribal Vengeance quest. She deals physical and fire damage, resists fire, and takes extra from cold.
beginner.whyItMatters: It is a quest fight, so the act waits on it, and her fire resistance means the obvious answer to a fire-themed boss is the wrong one here.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Around level 36 with fire resistance sorted. Cold damage cuts the fight short if you have any available.

name: Ignatia, the Flame-Sworn
description: One of two possible bosses at the end of the Alpine Ridge map, in the endgame layer at level 65 and above.

beginner.whatItIs: One of two possible bosses at the end of the Alpine Ridge map, in the endgame layer at level 65 and above.
beginner.whyItMatters: Alpine Ridge can end in either Ignatia or Gelida, and the two pull in opposite directions on element, so the map is a reminder that a boss room is not always the fight you expected.
beginner.whenToUseIt: On an Alpine Ridge map. Carrying resistance to both fire and cold rather than specialising is what makes either outcome routine.

name: Igrulog, the Incubator Queen
description: An encounter boss that appears in maps containing an abyss, rather than at the end of a fixed map layout.

beginner.whatItIs: An encounter boss that appears in maps containing an abyss, rather than at the end of a fixed map layout.
beginner.whyItMatters: Abyss content spawns waves of enemies before the boss arrives, so you fight her with whatever health and flask charges the waves left you.
beginner.whenToUseIt: When you run an abyss to its end in a map. If the waves have already worn you down, finishing the abyss is a choice rather than an obligation.

name: Iktab, the Deathlord
description: A level 25 Act 2 boss in the Bone Pits, part of the Theft of Ivory quest. It resists fire damage.

beginner.whatItIs: A level 25 Act 2 boss in the Bone Pits, part of the Theft of Ivory quest. It resists fire damage.
beginner.whyItMatters: The Bone Pits hold both Iktab and Ekbab, so the zone is a double boss commitment rather than a single fight, which matters when your portals are limited.
beginner.whenToUseIt: At level 25 or above, after clearing enough of the zone to have flasks and experience in hand. A non-fire damage source shortens it.

name: Imitation Triumph
description: An encounter fought inside Atziri's Temple, one of several set-piece opponents in that area.

beginner.whatItIs: An encounter fought inside Atziri's Temple, one of several set-piece opponents in that area.
beginner.whyItMatters: The temple is built as a gauntlet, so each encounter drains resources that the next one assumes you still have.
beginner.whenToUseIt: As part of a temple run. Pace yourself rather than treating the earlier encounters as filler.

name: Incarnation of Death
description: The map boss of the Penitentiary, in the endgame layer at level 65 and above.

beginner.whatItIs: The map boss of the Penitentiary, in the endgame layer at level 65 and above.

beginner.whenToUseIt: On a Penitentiary map. Position yourself with an exit route in mind before the fight opens rather than after it does.

name: Ishtaroth, the Perennial
description: The boss at the end of the Oasis map, part of the endgame content at level 65 and above.

beginner.whatItIs: The boss at the end of the Oasis map, part of the endgame content at level 65 and above.
beginner.whyItMatters: Open desert arenas give you room to move, which makes this a fair place to practise a boss pattern you have been dying to in tighter maps.
beginner.whenToUseIt: During atlas progression on an Oasis map. Use the space rather than fighting from one spot.

name: Isolde of the White Shroud
description: A level 54 named enemy in the Scorched Farmlands, fought during the Recruit the Ezomytes interlude quest. She resists cold and takes extra from fire.

beginner.whatItIs: A level 54 named enemy in the Scorched Farmlands, fought during the Recruit the Ezomytes interlude quest. She resists cold and takes extra from fire.
beginner.whyItMatters: She is the mirror of Heldra in the same zone: what counters one is exactly what the other shrugs off, so the farmlands reward a character carrying two damage options.
beginner.whenToUseIt: At level 54 or above. Fire damage is the direct answer here, and cold is the answer next door.

name: It That Was Esh
description: A level 78 and above boss in the Hive Colony. It deals physical, lightning and chaos damage using projectiles, projectile barrages, portal blasts, dashes, spawned orbs and a rolling lightning nova, and it cannot be fully slowed.

beginner.whenToUseIt: Once you are level 78 or above with lightning and chaos resistance handled. Learn to move through the projectile patterns before you commit expensive attempts.

name: It That Was Tul
description: A level 78 and above boss in the Hive Colony that fights with a shield. It deals physical and cold damage through triple melee combos, shield thrusts, slams and throws, tentacle attacks and an ice shower, and it cannot be fully slowed.

beginner.whatItIs: A level 78 and above boss in the Hive Colony that fights with a shield. It deals physical and cold damage through triple melee combos, shield thrusts, slams and throws, tentacle attacks and an ice shower, and it cannot be fully slowed.
beginner.whyItMatters: Where its Hive Colony counterpart fights at range, this one closes and combos, so the same zone asks for two different defensive habits from you in one run.
beginner.whenToUseIt: At level 78 or above with cold resistance capped and freeze avoidance in mind. Break the melee combo by moving early rather than after the first hit lands.

name: Jamanra, the Abomination
description: The Act 2 finale aboard the Dreadnought. He deals lightning and physical damage, carries thirty percent resistance to fire, lightning and physical, and takes thirty percent extra damage from cold.

beginner.whatItIs: The Act 2 finale aboard the Dreadnought. He deals lightning and physical damage, carries thirty percent resistance to fire, lightning and physical, and takes thirty percent extra damage from cold.
beginner.whyItMatters: This is the second form of the Act 2 antagonist and the fight that ends the act, and the stated minus thirty percent cold resistance is a rare explicit invitation to bring a specific element.
beginner.whenToUseIt: At the end of Act 2, with lightning resistance capped. If you have any cold damage available, this is the fight that rewards it directly.

name: Jamanra, the Risen King
description: The earlier Act 2 confrontation at the Halani Gates. He deals lightning and physical damage, resists fire, lightning and physical, and takes extra from cold.

beginner.whatItIs: The earlier Act 2 confrontation at the Halani Gates. He deals lightning and physical damage, resists fire, lightning and physical, and takes extra from cold.

beginner.whenToUseIt: On the normal Act 2 route. Treat it as a rehearsal and note which of his attacks caught you out, because you will see them again.

name: Kabala, Constrictor Queen
description: An Act 2 boss found in Keth, in the desert stretch of the campaign.

beginner.whatItIs: An Act 2 boss found in Keth, in the desert stretch of the campaign.
beginner.whyItMatters: Act 2 is where a character that skipped gear upgrades in Act 1 starts to fall behind, and a mid-act boss is where that gap becomes obvious.
beginner.whenToUseIt: On the Act 2 route through Keth. If the fight stalls, check your weapon damage against your level before blaming the fight.

name: Karash, The Dune Dweller
description: The map boss of the Mesa map, part of the endgame layer at level 65 and above.

beginner.whatItIs: The map boss of the Mesa map, part of the endgame layer at level 65 and above.
beginner.whyItMatters: Clearing the boss is what marks a map complete, so skipping it leaves the run unfinished no matter how much of the layout you cleared.
beginner.whenToUseIt: On a Mesa map during atlas progression. Finish the boss before opening the map exit rather than after.

name: Ketzuli, High Priest of the Sun
page: Ketzuli, High Priest of the Sun
description: A level 42 Act 3 boss in the Temple of Kopec, fought during the Legacy of the Vaal quest. He deals fire damage with firebolts, lasers, sun orbs, blazing salvos, scorching rays, a wormhole, a dash combo and a dense projectile phase, and he resists fire and cold.

beginner.whatItIs: A level 42 Act 3 boss in the Temple of Kopec, fought during the Legacy of the Vaal quest. He deals fire damage with firebolts, lasers, sun orbs, blazing salvos, scorching rays, a wormhole, a dash combo and a dense projectile phase, and he resists fire and cold.
beginner.whyItMatters: The projectile phase fills the arena, which makes it a movement test at the exact point in Act 3 where many characters are still standing still to attack. His fire resistance also removes the obvious counter to a fire boss.
beginner.whenToUseIt: At level 42 or above with fire resistance capped. Practise moving during the dense projectile phase instead of trying to damage through it.

name: Kosis, The Revelation

beginner.whatItIs: An encounter boss rather than a fixed zone boss, so it appears through content you trigger instead of at the end of a set area.

beginner.whenToUseIt: When the encounter appears. Reset your position and let cooldowns come back before you engage rather than fighting from where you were standing.

name: Krutog, Lord of Kin
quest:
Land of the Kin
Trial of the Ancestors (Quest)

name: Lachlann of Endless Lament
description: A level 7 Act 1 boss in the Cemetery of the Eternals, fought during the Sorrow Among Stones quest. He deals physical damage and resists physical damage.

beginner.whatItIs: A level 7 Act 1 boss in the Cemetery of the Eternals, fought during the Sorrow Among Stones quest. He deals physical damage and resists physical damage.
beginner.whyItMatters: A physical-resistant boss this early is a deliberate lesson: the weapon you have been swinging since level 1 is not a universal answer, and a support gem or an elemental skill will change the fight.
beginner.whenToUseIt: At level 7 or above. If you already have any elemental damage attached to your attack, this is the fight where you will feel it working.

name: Lady Elswyth
description: A named enemy at the Holten Estate, part of the interlude content that sits between the main acts. She resists fire and physical damage.

beginner.whatItIs: A named enemy at the Holten Estate, part of the interlude content that sits between the main acts. She resists fire and physical damage.
beginner.whyItMatters: The Holten area holds several named fights with overlapping fire and physical resistance, so a character built around one of those two spends the whole area fighting uphill.
beginner.whenToUseIt: When the Holten Estate is on your route. Bring cold or lightning damage if you have the option, and clear the surrounding area first so the fight starts clean.

name: Lord of the Pit
description: One of the bosses that can end the Sulphuric Caverns map, in the endgame layer at level 65 and above.

beginner.whatItIs: One of the bosses that can end the Sulphuric Caverns map, in the endgame layer at level 65 and above.
beginner.whyItMatters: Sulphuric Caverns can also finish with the Bone Colossus, so the same map name does not always mean the same fight waiting at the end.
beginner.whenToUseIt: On a Sulphuric Caverns map. Approach the boss arena expecting either outcome rather than committing to a plan before you see which one spawned.

name: Lythara, the Wayward Spear
description: A named enemy at Kriar Village in the interlude content between acts. She resists cold, lightning, fire and physical damage and takes extra from chaos.

beginner.whatItIs: A named enemy at Kriar Village in the interlude content between acts. She resists cold, lightning, fire and physical damage and takes extra from chaos.
beginner.whyItMatters: Resisting four damage types at once leaves chaos as the single opening, which is unusual and makes this a fight where the answer is a damage type rather than more gear.
beginner.whenToUseIt: When Kriar Village comes up. If you have any chaos or poison damage at all, this is the place to use it; without one, expect a long fight.

name: Malgor, the Nautilord
description: A map boss appearing at the end of the Port and Flotsam maps, part of the endgame content at level 65 and above.

beginner.whatItIs: A map boss appearing at the end of the Port and Flotsam maps, part of the endgame content at level 65 and above.
beginner.whyItMatters: Coastal map layouts often break the arena into narrow walkways, so a fight that would be simple in open ground becomes a positioning problem.
beginner.whenToUseIt: On a Port or Flotsam map. Fight from the widest piece of ground you can find rather than on the walkway you arrived along.

name: Manassa, the Serpent Queen
description: A map boss that appears across the Steaming Springs, Confluence and Spring maps in the endgame layer at level 65 and above.

beginner.whatItIs: A map boss that appears across the Steaming Springs, Confluence and Spring maps in the endgame layer at level 65 and above.
beginner.whyItMatters: She anchors three separate map layouts, so she turns up frequently in atlas running and is worth learning properly rather than muddling through.
beginner.whenToUseIt: On any of those three maps. Since you will see her repeatedly, treat the first attempt as the one where you actually watch her attacks.

name: Manoki, the Chosen
description: The boss of the Jade Isles map, part of the endgame map layer at level 65 and above.

beginner.whatItIs: The boss of the Jade Isles map, part of the endgame map layer at level 65 and above.
beginner.whyItMatters: A map only counts as completed once its boss falls, so this fight is the step that converts a cleared layout into atlas progress.
beginner.whenToUseIt: On a Jade Isles map during normal endgame running. Check the map modifiers before entering, since they apply to the boss too.

name: Master Flesh Surgeon
description: One of the named opponents inside Atziri's Temple, fought as a set-piece encounter rather than at the end of a map.

beginner.whatItIs: One of the named opponents inside Atziri's Temple, fought as a set-piece encounter rather than at the end of a map.
beginner.whyItMatters: The temple runs several of these encounters back to back, so the resource you actually need is flask charges and cooldowns rather than raw damage.
beginner.whenToUseIt: During a temple run. If an earlier encounter left you low, take the time to recover before triggering this one.

name: Master Thaumaturge
description: A caster-themed named opponent found in Atziri's Temple, fought as one of the temple's encounters.

beginner.whatItIs: A caster-themed named opponent found in Atziri's Temple, fought as one of the temple's encounters.
beginner.whyItMatters: The data recorded for this fight lists no resistance or weakness, which means there is no element to exploit and the fight is decided by your defences and your uptime.
beginner.whenToUseIt: As part of working through the temple. Keep your distance closed or opened deliberately rather than drifting into the middle of the arena.

name: Masterwork Smith
description: A smith-themed named opponent inside Atziri's Temple, one of the encounters the area is built around.

beginner.whatItIs: A smith-themed named opponent inside Atziri's Temple, one of the encounters the area is built around.
beginner.whyItMatters: Temple encounters are all optional in the sense that you chose to be there, so the honest question is whether your character is ready for a sequence of fights rather than one.
beginner.whenToUseIt: On a temple run, with resistances capped. Leave if the sequence is going badly rather than spending every portal proving a point.

name: Mektul, the Forgemaster
description: A level 41 Act 3 boss in the Molten Vault, fought during the Treasures of Utzaal quest. He deals fire and physical damage, resists fire, takes extra from cold, and is empowered by molten gold during the fight.

beginner.whatItIs: A level 41 Act 3 boss in the Molten Vault, fought during the Treasures of Utzaal quest. He deals fire and physical damage, resists fire, takes extra from cold, and is empowered by molten gold during the fight.
beginner.whyItMatters: The molten gold buff means his threat grows as the fight goes on, so a slow damage build gets punished for taking its time. His fire resistance also blocks the obvious counter to a forge boss.
beginner.whenToUseIt: At level 41 or above with fire resistance capped. Cold damage shortens the fight, which is the real way to limit how far the empowerment gets.

name: Meltwax, Mockery of Faith
description: The boss of the Crypt map in the endgame layer, fought at level 65 and above.

beginner.whatItIs: The boss of the Crypt map in the endgame layer, fought at level 65 and above.
beginner.whyItMatters: Crypt layouts are tight and corridor-heavy, which removes the room a lot of builds rely on to reset between attacks.
beginner.whenToUseIt: On a Crypt map. Pull the boss back to the widest chamber you passed rather than fighting where it stands.

name: Mighty Silverfist
description: A level 34 Act 3 boss in the Jungle Ruins. It deals physical damage and resists physical damage.

beginner.whatItIs: A level 34 Act 3 boss in the Jungle Ruins. It deals physical damage and resists physical damage.
beginner.whyItMatters: A physical boss with physical resistance is the campaign asking whether you ever added an element to your attack, and Act 3 is where that answer starts to matter for clear speed as well as bosses.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Around level 34. If a physical weapon is all you have, expect the fight to be long but survivable, and take the hint about your next gem.

name: Morvak, the Infernal
description: The map boss of the Canyon map, part of the endgame layer at level 65 and above.

beginner.whatItIs: The map boss of the Canyon map, part of the endgame layer at level 65 and above.
beginner.whyItMatters: Fire-themed endgame bosses are where an uncapped fire resistance stops being a small inefficiency and starts being the reason a run ends.
beginner.whenToUseIt: On a Canyon map with fire resistance at the cap. If the map itself rolled added fire damage, consider rerolling it instead.

name: Morwyn, the Kinslayer
description: The boss at the end of the Azmerian Ranges map, in the endgame content at level 65 and above.

beginner.whatItIs: The boss at the end of the Azmerian Ranges map, in the endgame content at level 65 and above.
beginner.whyItMatters: Map bosses are the reliable part of an endgame run, so building a routine around killing them rather than racing the layout is what makes atlas progress steady.
beginner.whenToUseIt: During normal map running. Finish the layout, then take the boss with full flasks rather than the other way around.

name: Murtagh, the Engorged
description: One of the two possible bosses of the Woodland map at level 65 and above. He swipes, swings a log, sunders the ground, charges, and summons drowned enemies.

beginner.whatItIs: One of the two possible bosses of the Woodland map at level 65 and above. He swipes, swings a log, sunders the ground, charges, and summons drowned enemies.
beginner.whyItMatters: He shares his attack set with several campaign and map monsters of the same family, so the pattern you learn here transfers directly to the others.
beginner.whenToUseIt: On a Woodland map. Handle the summoned drowned first, because letting them stack turns a manageable fight into a surround.

name: Oloton, the Remorseless
description: The boss of the Lofty Summit map at level 65 and above. He deals physical and fire damage, resists physical and fire, and takes extra from cold.

beginner.whatItIs: The boss of the Lofty Summit map at level 65 and above. He deals physical and fire damage, resists physical and fire, and takes extra from cold.
beginner.whyItMatters: His resistance and his damage are the same two types, so a physical or fire build both deals less and takes more in the same fight.
beginner.whenToUseIt: On a Lofty Summit map with fire resistance capped. Cold damage is the stated opening and it is worth swapping a gem for.

name: Oswin, the Dread Warden

beginner.whenToUseIt: When Wolvenhold is on your route. There is no quest clock on it, so come back a level or two higher if the first attempt goes badly.

name: Pirasha, the Forgotten Prisoner
description: The map boss of the Fortress map, part of the endgame layer at level 65 and above.

beginner.whatItIs: The map boss of the Fortress map, part of the endgame layer at level 65 and above.
beginner.whyItMatters: Fortress layouts funnel you through gates and courtyards, so you often arrive at the boss with less room and fewer flask charges than you planned for.
beginner.whenToUseIt: On a Fortress map. Take a moment at the arena entrance to recover before engaging rather than walking straight in.

name: Quadrilla Sergeant
description: A named enemy summoned by activating an Ancient Beacon rather than found in a fixed location.

beginner.whatItIs: A named enemy summoned by activating an Ancient Beacon rather than found in a fixed location.
beginner.whyItMatters: Beacon fights are entirely opt-in, so they are a safe way to add difficulty on your own schedule instead of having it handed to you by the campaign.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Light the beacon when your character is fresh. Skipping it costs you nothing except the reward.

name: Queen in the Mists
sourceStatBlock: Not published on poe2wiki yet - the source page carries no stat box, so this fight's level, location, resistances, weaknesses and attacks are unknown here rather than absent.
description: An encounter boss tied to triggered content rather than to a fixed zone, and related in name to the King in the Mists fights.

beginner.whatItIs: An encounter boss tied to triggered content rather than to a fixed zone, and related in name to the King in the Mists fights.

name: Rafiq of the Frozen Spring
description: A level 45 and above boss in the Trial of the Sekhemas, part of the ascendancy trial line. It fights with mace strikes, mace slams, heavy slams and a marker slam that telegraphs where it will land.

beginner.whyItMatters: The marker slam tells you exactly where not to stand, so this fight rewards reading the ground rather than reacting to the boss. It also stands between you and ascendancy points.
beginner.whenToUseIt: At level 45 or above, with your honour still healthy from the earlier floors. Step out of the marked ground rather than trying to tank the slam.

name: Rakkar, the Frozen Talon
description: A named enemy in the Glacial Tarn and Frozen Falls areas of the interlude content. It resists cold and takes extra from both fire and lightning.

beginner.whatItIs: A named enemy in the Glacial Tarn and Frozen Falls areas of the interlude content. It resists cold and takes extra from both fire and lightning.
beginner.whyItMatters: Two listed weaknesses is generous, so this is a fight where almost any elemental option other than cold will make quick work of it.
beginner.whenToUseIt: When either of those frozen areas is on your route. Leave your cold skills alone here and use anything else you carry.

name: Rathbreaker
description: A level 16 Act 2 boss in the Vastiri Outskirts, fought during the Earning Passage quest. It deals physical damage with slash combos, a spear rush, a sword slash and a sword slam, resists cold by thirty percent, and takes thirty percent extra damage from fire.

beginner.whatItIs: A level 16 Act 2 boss in the Vastiri Outskirts, fought during the Earning Passage quest. It deals physical damage with slash combos, a spear rush, a sword slash and a sword slam, resists cold by thirty percent, and takes thirty percent extra damage from fire.
beginner.whyItMatters: It is one of the first bosses whose weakness is stated as a clear number rather than implied, which makes it a good place to see how much a matching damage type actually changes a fight.
beginner.whenToUseIt: At level 16 or above with a fire source if you have one. Sidestep the spear rush rather than trying to outrun it along its line.

name: Rattlecage, the Earthbreaker
locations: Trial of the Sekhemas, Crimson Shores
description: A level 22 boss in the Trial of the Sekhemas and the Crimson Shores. It deals physical damage through explosive bursts, slams, fissure slams and rockslides, resists fire, lightning and physical, and takes extra from cold.

beginner.whatItIs: A level 22 boss in the Trial of the Sekhemas and the Crimson Shores. It deals physical damage through explosive bursts, slams, fissure slams and rockslides, resists fire, lightning and physical, and takes extra from cold.
beginner.whyItMatters: Most of what it throws comes up out of the ground, so movement matters more than mitigation. The exception is the rockslide it starts using below a third life, which falls from above instead, and it appears early enough that it is many players' first real ascendancy trial boss.
beginner.whenToUseIt: At level 22 or above. Keep moving between slams and use cold damage if you have it, since fire, lightning and physical are all blunted.

name: Riona, Winter's Cackle
description: A map boss appearing in the Mire and Frozen Falls maps at level 65 and above. She deals cold damage and resists cold damage.

beginner.whatItIs: A map boss appearing in the Mire and Frozen Falls maps at level 65 and above. She deals cold damage and resists cold damage.
beginner.whyItMatters: Dealing and resisting the same element means a cold build gets the worst of both sides here, taking more and dealing less at once.
beginner.whenToUseIt: On a Mire or Frozen Falls map with cold resistance capped and freeze avoidance in mind. Bring a non-cold damage source.

name: Rootdredge
description: A level 33 Act 3 boss in the Sandswept Marsh. It resists physical and cold damage.

beginner.whatItIs: A level 33 Act 3 boss in the Sandswept Marsh. It resists physical and cold damage.
beginner.whyItMatters: Physical and cold together cover the two damage types most melee characters are running by Act 3, which makes this a common place for a levelling character to stall.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Around level 33. If your damage is physical or cold, a fire or lightning option will change the fight more than another gear swap would.

name: Rootgrasp, the Hateful Forest
description: The map boss of the Spider Woods map at level 65 and above. It deals physical damage, resists cold by thirty percent, and takes fifty percent extra damage from fire.

beginner.whatItIs: The map boss of the Spider Woods map at level 65 and above. It deals physical damage, resists cold by thirty percent, and takes fifty percent extra damage from fire.
beginner.whyItMatters: A stated minus fifty percent fire resistance is a large opening for an endgame boss, so a fire source turns this from a long fight into a short one.
beginner.whenToUseIt: On a Spider Woods map. If you carry any fire damage, this is a fight worth swapping it in for.

name: Royal Blood Priest
description: One of the Vaal royal court opponents fought inside Atziri's Temple as a set-piece encounter.

beginner.whatItIs: One of the Vaal royal court opponents fought inside Atziri's Temple as a set-piece encounter.
beginner.whyItMatters: The temple's court encounters come as a group, so the run asks for endurance across several fights rather than a single push.
beginner.whenToUseIt: During a temple run, once earlier encounters have not left you low. Recover between fights rather than chaining them.

name: Royal Colossus
description: A large construct summoned by activating an Ancient Beacon rather than found in a fixed area.

beginner.whatItIs: A large construct summoned by activating an Ancient Beacon rather than found in a fixed area.
beginner.whyItMatters: Beacon spawns scale with the content you are running, so the same trigger can be routine in one map and dangerous in another.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Light the beacon when the map around you is already cleared. Fighting a summoned construct while a pack chases you is the avoidable version of this fight.

name: Royal Commander
description: A Vaal officer fought as one of the set-piece encounters inside Atziri's Temple.

beginner.whatItIs: A Vaal officer fought as one of the set-piece encounters inside Atziri's Temple.
beginner.whyItMatters: Officer-type opponents in this game tend to arrive with escorts, so the fight is usually about controlling what is around the boss as much as the boss itself.
beginner.whenToUseIt: During a temple run. Deal with any escort before committing your damage cooldowns to the commander.

name: Royal Sentinel
description: A guardian summoned by activating an Ancient Beacon, rather than an enemy tied to a fixed zone.

beginner.whatItIs: A guardian summoned by activating an Ancient Beacon, rather than an enemy tied to a fixed zone.
beginner.whyItMatters: Every beacon fight is a choice you make, so it is a clean way to test a new build against something dangerous without risking campaign or map progress.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Trigger it when you want the fight. If you are testing gear, do it here rather than on a boss that costs you a portal to retry.

name: Royal Spy Master
description: One of the Vaal court opponents encountered inside Atziri's Temple.

beginner.whatItIs: One of the Vaal court opponents encountered inside Atziri's Temple.
beginner.whyItMatters: The source records no resistance, weakness or skill list for this fight, which means there is nothing to counter-pick and the outcome rests on your defences.
beginner.whenToUseIt: As part of a temple run, with all three elemental resistances capped. Treat an unknown profile as a reason to play carefully rather than to skip it.

name: Rudja, the Dread Engineer

beginner.whatItIs: A level 18 Act 2 boss in the Mawdun Mine, fought during the Trail of Corruption quest. She deals physical and fire damage and resists fire.
beginner.whyItMatters: It is a required quest fight early in Act 2, at the point where many characters are still wearing Act 1 gear and have not topped up their fire resistance.
beginner.whenToUseIt: At level 18 or above, after checking that fire resistance is not negative. A single resistance ring here is worth more than a damage upgrade.

name: Saphira, The Dread Consort

beginner.whatItIs: A map boss found at the end of the Grimhaven and Epitaph maps in the endgame layer at level 65 and above.

beginner.whatItIs: The map boss of the Castaway map in the endgame layer, fought at level 65 and above.
beginner.whyItMatters: Killing the boss is what completes a map, so it is the step that converts a cleared layout into progress on your atlas.
beginner.whenToUseIt: On a Castaway map during normal endgame running. Enter the boss area with your flasks charged.

name: Torvian, Hand of the Saviour
skillsPartialReason: The source page lists 3 further attacks in a layout this extractor cannot read a name out of, so this list is incomplete.
description: A level 52 Act 4 boss at Arastas, fought during the Search quest. He resists physical damage.

beginner.whatItIs: A level 52 Act 4 boss at Arastas, fought during the Search quest. He resists physical damage.
beginner.whyItMatters: Physical resistance this late in the campaign means a weapon build without any added element is running at reduced output at exactly the point the game stops being forgiving.
beginner.whenToUseIt: At level 52 or above. If your attack has no elemental component by now, adding one will do more here than another gear upgrade.

name: Tycho, the Black Praetor
description: The map boss of the Necropolis map, in the endgame layer at level 65 and above.

beginner.whatItIs: The map boss of the Necropolis map, in the endgame layer at level 65 and above.
beginner.whyItMatters: Endgame bosses take the map's rolled modifiers with them, so the same fight can be routine on one map and dangerous on another.
beginner.whenToUseIt: On a Necropolis map. Read the modifiers before you enter rather than discovering them in the boss arena.

name: Unchained Beast
description: A creature released by activating an Ancient Beacon rather than found in a fixed location.

beginner.whatItIs: A creature released by activating an Ancient Beacon rather than found in a fixed location.
beginner.whyItMatters: Beacon fights are triggered by you, so their timing is a decision rather than an ambush, which is rare enough to be worth using deliberately.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Light the beacon once the area around you is clear and your cooldowns are up. There is no benefit to triggering it under pressure.

name: Uxmal, the Beastlord
description: A level 40 and above boss in the Temple of Chaos, part of the Trial of Chaos ascendancy line. It deals physical, fire, cold, lightning and chaos damage and resists fire, cold and lightning.

beginner.whatItIs: A level 40 and above boss in the Temple of Chaos, part of the Trial of Chaos ascendancy line. It deals physical, fire, cold, lightning and chaos damage and resists fire, cold and lightning.
beginner.whyItMatters: It attacks with five different damage types while resisting three of them, so there is no single defence to stack and no easy element to counter with. Clearing it is part of earning ascendancy points.
beginner.whenToUseIt: At level 40 or above with all three elemental resistances capped and chaos resistance not deeply negative. Broad defences beat specialised ones here.

name: Vandroth, Blackblooded Enslaver
description: An encounter boss in the Dark Domain. It fights with a crystalshatter attack, a charge, a vomit spray and a submerge that takes it out of reach.

beginner.whatItIs: An encounter boss in the Dark Domain. It fights with a crystalshatter attack, a charge, a vomit spray and a submerge that takes it out of reach.
beginner.whyItMatters: The submerge controls when the fight is available to you, so your damage has to fit into the windows it gives rather than run continuously.
beginner.whenToUseIt: When the Dark Domain encounter is available. Hold your damage cooldowns for the moment it resurfaces rather than spending them on an empty arena.

name: Vastweld, the Colossal Guardian
description: The map boss of the Forge map at level 65 and above. It deals physical and fire damage, resists physical and fire, and takes extra from cold.

beginner.whatItIs: The map boss of the Forge map at level 65 and above. It deals physical and fire damage, resists physical and fire, and takes extra from cold.
beginner.whyItMatters: Its resistances and its damage are the same two types, so a fire or physical build both deals less and takes more, while cold is a stated opening.
beginner.whenToUseIt: On a Forge map with fire resistance capped. If you have a cold damage option, this is a fight worth swapping it in for.

name: Vessel of Kulemak
description: A level 80 to 82 pinnacle-tier encounter in the Black Cathedral. Its recorded attacks are a melee swipe and a cleave that covers the whole arena.

beginner.whatItIs: A level 80 to 82 pinnacle-tier encounter in the Black Cathedral. Its recorded attacks are a melee swipe and a cleave that covers the whole arena.
beginner.whyItMatters: An arena-wide attack cannot be avoided by moving away from the boss, so surviving it is a matter of defences and timing rather than positioning.
beginner.whenToUseIt: At level 80 or above with a finished character. Plan for the arena-wide cleave specifically rather than treating it as another attack to sidestep.

name: Veynar, the Frostbane
description: The map boss of the Bastille map, part of the endgame map layer at level 65 and above.

beginner.whatItIs: The map boss of the Bastille map, part of the endgame map layer at level 65 and above.
beginner.whyItMatters: A map counts as finished only when its boss falls, so this fight is the difference between a run that advances your atlas and one that simply used up a map.
beginner.whenToUseIt: On a Bastille map during endgame progression. Enter the arena with flask charges rather than spending them on the approach.

name: Viper Napuatzi
description: A level 43 Act 3 boss in Utzaal, fought during the Legacy of the Vaal quest. She deals physical, chaos and fire damage and resists fire, cold, lightning and physical.

beginner.whatItIs: A level 43 Act 3 boss in Utzaal, fought during the Legacy of the Vaal quest. She deals physical, chaos and fire damage and resists fire, cold, lightning and physical.
beginner.whyItMatters: Resisting all four of those damage types leaves nothing to counter-pick, and her chaos damage bypasses energy shield, so both your offence and one of your defensive layers are blunted at once.
beginner.whenToUseIt: At level 43 or above with capped elemental resistances and life rather than shield alone carrying you. Expect a long fight regardless of what you brought.

name: Volkhar, the Emberborn
description: The map boss of the Crimson Shores map in the endgame layer, fought at level 65 and above.

beginner.whatItIs: The map boss of the Crimson Shores map in the endgame layer, fought at level 65 and above.
beginner.whyItMatters: Crimson Shores also appears as a location for an early ascendancy trial boss, so the same name can mean very different content depending on where you meet it.
beginner.whenToUseIt: On a Crimson Shores map at level 65 or above. Do not assume it plays like the trial fight of the same setting.

name: Vornas, the Fell Flame
description: A named enemy at the Galai Gates in the interlude content between acts. He resists fire and physical damage and takes extra from cold and lightning.

beginner.whatItIs: A named enemy at the Galai Gates in the interlude content between acts. He resists fire and physical damage and takes extra from cold and lightning.
beginner.whyItMatters: Two resistances and two weaknesses make this a clean demonstration of how much damage type selection matters, since the same character can feel weak or strong here purely on gem choice.
beginner.whenToUseIt: When the Galai Gates are on your route. Lead with cold or lightning rather than your physical attack.

name: Vorrik, The Infernal Engineer
description: A map boss found in the Slick and Mineshaft maps, part of the endgame layer at level 65 and above.

beginner.whatItIs: A map boss found in the Slick and Mineshaft maps, part of the endgame layer at level 65 and above.
beginner.whyItMatters: He anchors two map layouts, so he appears often enough in an atlas rotation that learning his pattern is worth the attention.
beginner.whenToUseIt: On either map during endgame running. Since you will see him repeatedly, use the first encounter to watch rather than to rush.

name: Xesht, We That Are One
description: A pinnacle-tier demon fought in the Twisted Domain, at level 79 as a quest and at level 82 in its regular form. It deals physical and chaos damage and resists fire, cold and lightning.

beginner.whatItIs: A pinnacle-tier demon fought in the Twisted Domain, at level 79 as a quest and at level 82 in its regular form. It deals physical and chaos damage and resists fire, cold and lightning.
beginner.whyItMatters: Resisting all three elements while dealing chaos damage means elemental builds lose offence and shield-based builds lose defence, so it asks for a well-rounded character rather than a specialised one.
beginner.whenToUseIt: At level 79 or above with chaos resistance handled and a real life pool. This is endgame content, not a step on the campaign route.

name: Xipocado, Royal Architect
description: One of the Vaal court opponents inside Atziri's Temple. It deals chaos and lightning damage.

beginner.whatItIs: One of the Vaal court opponents inside Atziri's Temple. It deals chaos and lightning damage.
beginner.whyItMatters: Chaos damage in a temple full of encounters is a slow drain rather than a single spike, so it wears down characters that rely on energy shield recharging between fights.
beginner.whenToUseIt: During a temple run with lightning resistance capped and chaos resistance not negative. Recover fully before triggering it.

name: Xyclucian, the Chimera
description: A level 36 Act 3 boss in the Chimeral Wetlands, fought during the Legacy of the Vaal quest.

beginner.whatItIs: A level 36 Act 3 boss in the Chimeral Wetlands, fought during the Legacy of the Vaal quest.
beginner.whyItMatters: It is a required quest fight in the middle of Act 3, at the point where the campaign stops tolerating gear that has not been replaced since Act 2.
beginner.whenToUseIt: At level 36 or above. If the fight stalls, compare your weapon damage against your character level before changing anything else.

name: Yama The White (boss)
description: An Act 4 boss found in the Halls of the Dead.

beginner.whatItIs: An Act 4 boss found in the Halls of the Dead.
beginner.whyItMatters: Act 4 sits at the end of the campaign, where enemy damage is tuned for capped resistances and an upgraded weapon rather than for whatever carried you through Act 3.
beginner.whenToUseIt: On the Act 4 route through the Halls of the Dead. Treat a quick death here as a gear signal rather than a skill problem.

name: Yaota, the Loathsome
description: The map boss of the Backwash map, part of the endgame layer at level 65 and above.

beginner.whatItIs: The map boss of the Backwash map, part of the endgame layer at level 65 and above.
beginner.whyItMatters: Endgame maps carry rolled modifiers that apply to the boss as well as the zone, so the same fight varies in difficulty from map to map.
beginner.whenToUseIt: On a Backwash map. Read the modifiers before entering rather than finding out during the fight.

name: Zahmir, the Blade Sovereign
description: The boss of the Sacred Reservoir map, in the endgame map layer at level 65 and above.

beginner.whatItIs: The boss of the Sacred Reservoir map, in the endgame map layer at level 65 and above.
beginner.whyItMatters: A blade-themed boss leans on fast melee sequences, which punishes standing still to finish your own attack animation.
beginner.whenToUseIt: On a Sacred Reservoir map. Break off your attack to move when a combo starts rather than committing to it.

name: Zalmarath, the Colossus
description: A level 27 Act 2 boss in the Titan Grotto, fought during the Crown of Stone quest. It deals physical and fire damage and resists physical damage.

beginner.whatItIs: A level 27 Act 2 boss in the Titan Grotto, fought during the Crown of Stone quest. It deals physical and fire damage and resists physical damage.
beginner.whyItMatters: It is a required quest fight that resists exactly the damage type most levelling melee characters are still relying on in Act 2.
beginner.whenToUseIt: At level 27 or above with fire resistance on your gear. An elemental damage source shortens the fight noticeably compared with a plain weapon.

name: Zar Wali, the Bone Tyrant
description: A map boss appearing in the Marrow and Hidden Grotto maps at level 65 and above. It resists physical and fire damage.

beginner.whatItIs: A map boss appearing in the Marrow and Hidden Grotto maps at level 65 and above. It resists physical and fire damage.
beginner.whyItMatters: Two resistances with no stated weakness means there is no counter-pick to make, so the fight is settled by your gear level and your movement.
beginner.whenToUseIt: On either map. If your damage is physical or fire, budget for a longer fight rather than expecting to burst it down.

name: Zarokh, the Temporal
description: A level 78 to 80 pinnacle boss at the end of the Trial of the Sekhemas. It deals physical damage through temporal traps, explosive rods, orb projectiles, slowing orbs and lightning tendrils, and it has a clock phase, with thirty percent resistance to fire, cold and lightning.

beginner.whatItIs: A level 78 to 80 pinnacle boss at the end of the Trial of the Sekhemas. It deals physical damage through temporal traps, explosive rods, orb projectiles, slowing orbs and lightning tendrils, and it has a clock phase, with thirty percent resistance to fire, cold and lightning.
beginner.whyItMatters: The clock phase and the slowing orbs change how fast you can act, so your usual movement timing stops working and has to be relearned inside the fight.
beginner.whenToUseIt: At level 78 or above, after you can clear the earlier Sekhemas floors with honour to spare. Learn the clock phase specifically before committing serious attempts.

name: Zekoa, The Headcrusher
description: A map boss found in the Riverside and Rupture maps, part of the endgame layer at level 65 and above.

beginner.whatItIs: A map boss found in the Riverside and Rupture maps, part of the endgame layer at level 65 and above.
beginner.whyItMatters: Because he anchors two layouts, he is part of the regular atlas rotation, and a fight you meet often is one where small mistakes accumulate into deaths.
beginner.whenToUseIt: On either map during endgame running. Keep treating it as a boss fight even after it becomes familiar.

name: Zelina, Blood Priestess
description: A named enemy in the Cuachic Vault, part of the interlude content between acts. She resists cold damage.

beginner.whatItIs: A named enemy in the Cuachic Vault, part of the interlude content between acts. She resists cold damage.
beginner.whyItMatters: The vault holds a matching blood priest with the same cold resistance, so it is a paired fight rather than a single one and a cold build is blunted twice over.
beginner.whenToUseIt: When the Cuachic Vault is on your route. Bring a damage type other than cold and expect to use it twice.

name: Zicoatl, Warden of the Core
description: A level 37 Act 3 boss in Jiquani's Sanctum. It resists fire and physical damage and takes extra from cold.

beginner.whatItIs: A level 37 Act 3 boss in Jiquani's Sanctum. It resists fire and physical damage and takes extra from cold.
beginner.whyItMatters: It shares its resistance profile with the boss of the neighbouring Machinarium, so the pair of zones asks the same question about your damage twice in a row.
beginner.whenToUseIt: Around level 37 on the Act 3 route. Cold damage is the stated opening for both fights in this part of the act.

name: Zolin, Blood Priest
description: A named enemy in the Cuachic Vault in the interlude content between acts. He resists cold damage.

beginner.whatItIs: A named enemy in the Cuachic Vault in the interlude content between acts. He resists cold damage.
beginner.whyItMatters: He is the counterpart to the blood priestess in the same vault, so you face the same cold resistance twice without a break in between.
beginner.whenToUseIt: When the Cuachic Vault comes up. Handle both priests with the same non-cold damage source rather than swapping between them.
